value: Stay strong
Days 61-90: beat complacency and relapse traps, finish the patch taper, reach 3 months
Day 61: Welcome to chapter four
Confidence is high right now, and that is exactly when guard can slip. This chapter keeps you sharp on the way to three months, and it is where you finish your nicotine taper entirely.
Know the complacency trap
Many relapses happen after the two month mark, not because life gets harder, but because people stop taking cravings seriously once they feel they have already won.
Name your current biggest risk
Write down the one situation most likely to challenge you in the next thirty days.
Set your chapter four goal
Pick one thing you want to stay alert about this month.
Day 62: The just-checking trap
Having one to test your willpower sounds like harmless curiosity. It is the addiction writing its own comeback.
Why testing yourself backfires

A test cigarette puts nicotine back in your body and wakes the little monster. It proves nothing except that the trap still works. The real test of freedom is not smoking one and feeling fine; it is not wanting one at all.
Honesty check
Write honestly whether the idea of just one to test yourself has crossed your mind lately. Naming the thought defuses it.
Day 63: Boredom, the long game
Boredom never fully retires, it just visits less often. Keep the toolkit oiled.
Refresh your boredom toolkit
Try a mini game you have not used in a while during a slow moment today.
Add one new boredom activity
Add one activity to your boredom list that you have never tried before.
Day 64: Nine weeks free
Nine weeks. Your old smoking schedule probably feels like someone else's calendar.
Claim your nine week badge
Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.
Nine week stats
Open your stats and review your streak, money saved and health markers.
Day 65: Celebration triggers again
Promotions, achievements and parties can quietly whisper the old way of celebrating.
Audit a recent good moment
Write about a recent piece of good news and whether any urge came with it.
Plan your three month celebration
Decide in advance how you will celebrate the three month milestone when it arrives, using saved money if you like.
Day 66: Holidays and special days
Special occasions, even small ones, carry old associations. A plan beats willpower every time.
Rate upcoming occasion risk
If a birthday, holiday or event is coming, rate how risky it feels.
Plan beats willpower
Walking into a special occasion with a plan for smoke breaks and toasts works far better than improvising against pressure in the moment.
Day 67: Old friends, old habits
Someone from your smoking past can resurface without warning: a reunion, an old coworker, a returning friend.
Name the person
Write about anyone from your past you associate strongly with smoking, even if you rarely see them.
Pre-decide your response
Decide now exactly what you will say and do if that person offers you a cigarette. Rehearsed answers do not wobble.
Day 68: Ten weeks, last patch week
Ten weeks free, and if you followed the standard taper, this is your final week wearing a patch.
Claim your ten week badge
Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.
Prepare for patch-free life

If you have finished about two weeks on the lowest strength, you can stop patches at the end of this week. Keep a small supply of lozenges for the following two or three weeks as a safety net for surprise cravings, and plan to phase those out too.
Day 69: Tiredness and low energy
Exhaustion lowers everyone's guard, including around old habits. Rest is a relapse-prevention tool.
Notice the tiredness link
Write whether you have noticed any connection between being very tired and thinking about cigarettes.
Rest on purpose
Use a relaxing sound for a few minutes today if you are feeling run down.
Day 70: Patch-free day
Seventy days, and for standard taper users, the first day with no patch at all. From today, any nicotine in your body is zero. The little monster is not just starving anymore; it is gone.
Mark the patch-free milestone
If today is your first patch-free day, expect a few quieter-than-feared days. Keep lozenges and your oral kit around as backup, and remember: any craving now is purely mental echo, not chemical need.
The little monster is dead

With no nicotine entering your body from any source, the physical addiction has nothing left to live on. Everything from here is habit memory and old beliefs, and you have been dismantling those for ten weeks.
Share a seventy day update
Post a quick update in the community about hitting seventy days.
Day 71: Watching for warning signs
Small warning signs, like more frequent thoughts about smoking, are worth catching early, especially in the week after stopping NRT.
Rate craving frequency
Rate how often you have thought about smoking in the past three days.
Add one extra tool this week
If cravings feel louder since dropping the patch, add one extra daily tool this week: a scheduled breathing session, an evening walk, or a community check-in.
Day 72: The mental bargaining trap
Just this once thoughts get more articulate over time. The risk underneath them never changes.
Know the bargaining pattern

The mind can build a beautiful case for one exception: special occasion, terrible day, just this once. However elegant the argument, the outcome is identical: the monster gets fed and the cycle restarts. There are no special-occasion cigarettes, only first cigarettes.
Write your counter-argument
Write one strong sentence to answer any just-this-once thought, ready in advance.
Day 73: Checking your why
Reconnecting with your original reason keeps it vivid instead of letting it fade into wallpaper.
Revisit your original reason
Write the main reason you quit, and whether it still feels as important now.
Watch the savings grow
Open your money saved tab and notice the total, now also free of NRT costs going forward.
Day 74: Eleven weeks free
One more week stands between you and three full months.
Claim your eleven week badge
Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.
Rate readiness for three months
Rate how ready you feel for the three month milestone.
Day 75: Helping someone else
Supporting another quitter strengthens your own resolve at the same time.
Support a newer quitter
Find someone in their first month and offer one piece of encouragement or advice.
What would you tell day one you
Write the single most useful thing you would tell yourself on day one, knowing what you know now.
Day 76: Physical activity boost
Stamina keeps improving well past the early months, and now with zero nicotine constricting your blood vessels.
See your stamina gains
By around three months, lung function has improved enough for many ex smokers that stairs and brisk walking feel noticeably easier.
Test your stamina
Do one physical activity today, even a short brisk walk, and notice the difference from your smoking days.
Day 77: Mental clarity check
Steadier focus is one of the most commonly reported gains at this stage, now that the withdrawal-relief rollercoaster is gone.
Notice your focus
Write whether your concentration or mental clarity feels different since you quit.
Rate your wellbeing
Rate how you feel overall today on a simple scale.
Day 78: Twelve weeks free
Three months are two days away.
Claim your twelve week badge
Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.
Finalize your three month plan
Decide exactly how you will mark three full months in two days.
Day 79: The night before
Tomorrow is a major milestone. Today is just about staying steady.
Scroll your whole journey
Open your stats and scroll through your entire history from day one to today.
What tomorrow means
Write a sentence or two about what reaching three months represents for you.
Day 80: Three months smoke free

Ninety days by the old count, three calendar months by any count: a quarter of a year without a single cigarette, and now without any nicotine at all. One of the biggest milestones in quitting, medically and mentally.
Claim your three month badge
Open your badges tab and collect this major milestone.
Three month transformation
By three months, lung function and circulation have generally improved substantially compared to when you smoked, and your body is running fully nicotine free.
Share the milestone
Post your three month update in the community.
Write your journey summary
A few sentences summarizing the road from day one to today.
Day 81: After the big milestone
Motivation often dips slightly right after a big milestone passes. Knowing that in advance makes it a shrug instead of a crisis.
The post-milestone dip
Motivation drops a little after a big goal simply because the immediate target is gone. It is normal and temporary.
Set the next target
Pick a new personal goal now that three months is behind you.
Day 82: Routine maintenance
The goal shifts from building habits to simply maintaining the ones that work.
List your core habits
Write the three or four replacement habits that have become most automatic.
Keep one habit fresh
Do one core replacement habit on purpose today, even without needing it.
Day 83: Long term money goal
Three months of unspent cigarette money is a real amount. Think bigger with it.
See your three month savings
Open your money saved tab and look at the total since day one.
Set a savings goal
Pick something specific to put your smoking money toward over the next few months.
Day 84: Phasing out the lozenges
If you kept lozenges as a post-patch safety net, this is a good week to start letting them go too.
Taper the last NRT

Start swapping nicotine lozenges for plain peppermints or sugar-free gum, cutting your daily lozenge count roughly in half this week and aiming for zero within two to three weeks. If cravings spike, slow down rather than white-knuckling; the exit still counts if it takes an extra week.
Rate how distant smoking feels
Rate how far away your smoking days feel compared to right after you quit.
Day 85: Boredom relapse watch
Even at this stage, plain boredom remains one of the sneakier triggers.
Boredom never fully retires
Even long-term ex smokers can feel an occasional pull in very boring stretches. Having a plan ready matters more than expecting the urge to vanish forever.
Refresh your distraction list
Update your boredom list with anything new you have discovered.
Day 86: Reflecting on identity
By now, many people simply are non smokers, rather than smokers holding a door shut.
The stranger test
Write how someone meeting you today, with no history, would describe your relationship with smoking.
Identity predicts success
Shifting from quitting smoker to simply non smoker in your own mind is one of the strongest predictors of staying smoke free long term.
Day 87: Shaping your own plan
Nearly three months of missions behind you. Time to notice what you actually still need.
Rate your tool usage
Rate how often you still use the craving toolkit compared to month one.
What do you need less of
Write which part of the plan you feel you need less support from now.
Day 88: Almost chapter five
The next chapter moves into identity, health wins, and confidence as a settled non smoker.
Preview chapter five
Chapter five focuses on identity as a non smoker, ongoing health wins, and finishing any remaining NRT so you are fully nicotine free.
Set a chapter five intention
Write one intention for how you want to think about yourself going into the next chapter.
Day 89: One day left in chapter four
Tomorrow wraps a chapter built around the highest complacency risk window, and you are exiting it with your streak intact.
A guard-down moment you caught
Write about a moment this chapter where you almost let your guard down but did not.
Rate chapter four
Rate how well you handled chapter four overall.

Ninety days behind you, patch behind you, and the riskiest complacency window passed with your streak intact. From here, the work shifts from staying strong to fully becoming who you are now.
